This page summarises the main results of the project. It is updated as new articles are published; the full list is in [Publications](publications.qmd).

## OG1 · The bias of the Gini index

**Results.** Monte Carlo studies with six distributions (Pareto, Dagum with $p=20$ and $p=0.5$, lognormal, Weibull and Gamma), Gini indices from 0.1 to 0.8 and different sample sizes. They can be reproduced with the [interactive bias explorer](simulation.qmd).

**Conclusions.**

- $\widehat{G}_n^{a}$ has **excessively large biases** in datasets with low inequality. Two equivalent solutions:
  a. replace $\widehat{F}_n(t)$ with the smoothed (mid-point) distribution function
  $$\widehat{F}_n^{*}(t)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in S}\left[\delta(y_i<t)+0.5\,\delta(y_i=t)\right],$$
  which gives the estimator $\widehat{G}_n^{b}$;
  b. subtract $1/n$ when there are no ties: $\widehat{G}_n^{b}=\widehat{G}_n^{a}-1/n$.
- **Skewness** has a significant effect on the bias of the three versions of the Gini index (hypothesis H1).
- In highly skewed distributions, **inequality** has a major effect on the bias of the three versions (hypothesis H2).

**Publications.** *Exploring and correcting the bias in the estimation of the Gini measure of inequality* (Muñoz, Moya-Fernández and Álvarez-Verdejo, *Sociological Methods & Research*); *A practical guide to proper estimation and inference of the Gini index by avoiding often encountered methodological pitfalls* (*Social Indicators Research*, 2026).

## OG2 · Missing data and the Gini index

**In progress.** The project analyses the impact of missing data on the Gini index under the three non-response mechanisms (MCAR, MAR and MNAR), and compares complete-case analysis, single imputation and multiple imputation. The [missing data simulator](missing-data.qmd) illustrates the patterns that motivate this objective:

- deleting the cases with missing data (**complete-case analysis**) is only safe when data are missing completely at random (MCAR);
- **mean imputation** always underestimates inequality, because all imputed values are equal;
- **deterministic regression imputation** also underestimates inequality, because it ignores the residual variability;
- **stochastic regression imputation** and **multiple imputation** remove most of the bias when the data are missing at random (MAR) and the imputation model includes the variables related to non-response;
- when non-response depends on income itself (**MNAR**), no standard method removes the bias.

**Working papers.** *The problem of missing data in strategic management research: critical issues, understanding and methodological insights* (Vendrell, Muñoz, Gomes and Lehman); *How to avoid common mistakes in water studies with missing data?* (Muñoz, Álvarez, Tortajada and Sarwar).

## OG3 · The R package giniVarCI

**Achieved.** The package [**giniVarCI**](software.qmd) is available on CRAN. It:

1. estimates the Gini index for samples from finite and infinite populations with all the expressions of the literature;
2. computes variances and confidence intervals with different methods (jackknife, linearisation, bootstrap, empirical likelihood);
3. computes the Gini index of continuous probability distributions (Beta, Burr, Dagum, F, Fisk, Gamma, lognormal, Pareto, etc.);
4. draws samples from continuous distributions with a Gini index set by the user;
5. uses *Rcpp*, so calculations are faster than in other packages that compute the Gini index.
